This is an introductory course to engineering fundamental of various energy sources including fossil fuel and renewable energy.

This course is designed to provide a broad introduction to global environmental challenges we face today. It will cover several global environmental topics such as climate change, biodiversity, marine pollution, hazardous waste and trans-boundary air pollution. It will also cover issues in environmental law and international trade law.

The course will introduce students to the main concepts of the global health field and enhance their understandings in the social, economic, cultural, legal, and political processes by which global health policy influences global health objectives. Students will be able to discuss the social, political and economic determinants of global health and identify the evolving national institutions, international organizations, private interests, and global partnerships structuring global health policy. Students will further analyze the ethical, moral and legal norms that frame global health governance and evaluate global health policy to address disease prevention and health promotion. Potential topics to be explored include basic research methods in global health, health systems and management, infectious diseases and epidemics, global nutrition and agriculture, child health, sexual and reproductive health, humanitarian aid, environmental health, conflict, culture, and gender, etc.

Management statistics is an introductory statistics course for students of management, business, and economics. This course covers principles and practices of statistics in the context of substantive, engaging, and up-to-date applications in management, business, and economics.

After learning basic French grammar, students will train in basic French speaking skills, including correct pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary practice, to help them develop their French communication skills.

This course is intended to enhance students who have chosen the Department of AI and Biomedical Engineering or wish to major in the field of AI Biomedical Engineering, which provides students with the opportunity to explore and choose their major correctly, and to design their curriculum and careers in the future.

This course serves as an introductory major course in Spatial Design, offering fundamental practical experience in English.

The primary objective of this course is to comprehensively understand various spatial environments where life occurs and to enhance the necessary perspectives, theoretical knowledge, and spatial design expression skills needed to create them. We aim to broaden our perspective on how we perceive spatial environments in our daily lives, foster creative thinking, interdisciplinary abilities, and expressive skills to create improved spaces.

Throughout this course, students will practice exercises that involve expressing spaces using architectural elements, with the goal of developing perceptual and creative potential in relation to spaces. Students will gain experience in the basic architectural language of form required to create spaces accommodating human behavior, analyze spatial meanings, and cultivate spatial expression abilities during the design process. Additionally, the course aims to enhance conceptual idea development, visual communication skills, and provide fundamental practice in spatial design, ultimately contributing to a broader understanding of architecture and interior design as a whole.

● to observe and gain an understanding of the physical characteristics of the spatial environments in which we reside
● to understand architects’ philosophy, design concepts, and spatial drawings through the examination of global architectural works
● to understand spatial scale and design elements while acquiring the skills necessary for architectural representation techniques and 3D model making (including sketching, drawing, diagrams, photography, collage, 3D study models, etc.).
● to foster the design development of spatial concept ideas and enhance visual communication skills
● to Acquire knowledge of spatial design methods, fundamental components, and the overall design process.

This course focuses on acquiring the fundamental and essential mathematical tools required for specialized studies in Biologics Engineering. Moving beyond general mathematical concepts, it specifically educates students on the core principles of differential equations, linear algebra, and basic statistics necessary for solving practical engineering problems such as bioreactor modeling, pharmacokinetic analysis, and biological system data processing. Students will strengthen their quantitative reasoning skills through this course, enabling them to analytically model and predict complex bioengineering phenomena using real-world examples from the biologics field.

This course is designed for students who have selected or are considering Biologics Engineering as their major. It aims to enhance their understanding of biomedical polymers, which serve as the fundamental basis for the delivery of biopharmaceutical raw materials. By taking this course, students will be provided with opportunities for proper academic exploration and informed major selection. Furthermore, it will establish a solid foundation in drug delivery systems (DDS), ensuring sufficient comprehension for future advanced coursework related to biopharmaceuticals.
